dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 31 May spike is DLR-104 and DLR-219's monthly annual-plan batch landing on the last day of the month"
"effective_event_date = dealer transaction date, posted_at = month-end"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Entitlement posting isn't confirmed in this data — only the cash/row/duplicate checks are evidenced"
"Duplicate revenue — no duplicate IDs, no repeated combos, exact reconciliation. Ruled out."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing

"Pull the entitlement log for these source events and confirm activation dates align with effective_event_date, and confirm revenue recognition uses the same field"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "It concentrates trend-pack activity at month-end, which is a reporting artifact worth flagging, not a control failure."
"Separately, flag to whoever owns the weekly trend pack that DLR-104/DLR-219 volume will always cluster at month-end by design"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Duplicate revenue ... Ruled out" is somewhat broader than the tested evidence: duplicate identifiers and repeated combinations were checked, but distinct identifiers could theoretically still represent duplicate economic events; entitlement impact remains unconfirmed.

"Manipulated/backdated reporting ... Ruled out" is stronger than the evidence supports. The spread of effective dates and repeated dealer pattern make manipulation less likely, but do not definitively exclude it.

"Pipeline defect / one-off glitch ... Ruled out" is also overstated. The pattern supports a recurring posting convention rather than a one-off glitch, but a systematic pipeline or field-mapping defect is not fully tested.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately considered duplicate revenue, manipulation, and a pipeline glitch, and it identified downstream event-time distortion. The main residual alternative it did not fully test is a systematic accounting or data-pipeline field-mapping defect—especially revenue or trend-pack logic using posted_at rather than effective_event_date—even if the dealer uploads themselves are legitimate.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and document the entitlement and revenue-recognition reconciliation for the 17 source events, including confirmation that downstream analytics and accounting use effective_event_date where appropriate; soften the categorical 'ruled out' language until those checks are complete.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South complaints fell ~30–40% after NovaIVR launch... tickets.csv (internal data)"
"Call volume stayed constant... service_events.csv"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "NovaIVR resolved common issues preemptively. Call log data show many IVR sessions ending in resolution (self-service) without creating a ticket."
"Causality: We infer IVR caused the drop, but proof would be comparing a matched control..."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Promising but inconclusive – don’t expand nationally yet."
"Data/reporting glitch: No anomalies seen in ticketing or call logs... Metrics passed reconciliation checks."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Continue the South pilot and measure carefully; hold off on national rollout."
"implement a short (e.g. one-month) trial in a second region as a control group"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "What share of South callers went through the new IVR versus speaking to an agent, and what proportion of IVR calls ended without a ticket?"
"How did overall call patterns change? (E.g. call volume, average wait time, or call abandonment in the South after NovaIVR...)"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "This rules out company-wide factors." Stable or seasonally normal complaint counts in other regions do not rule out all company-wide or South-specific confounders.
"Call volume stayed constant." The submission gives no field, cohort, query, or reported values supporting this claim.

"many IVR sessions ending in resolution (self-service) without creating a ticket." A session ending without case creation does not establish successful resolution; it may reflect abandonment or a capture failure.

"The IVR handles typical billing and service queries noted as common complaint drivers." The submission does not show the relevant IVR stages, error rates, or linkage between those sessions and later customer outcomes.
"Metrics passed reconciliation checks." No reconciliation method, fields, or results are provided.
"Instead, complaints across issue types fell and then stabilized at the lower level through the pilot period." This is asserted without category-level evidence or a reproducible comparison.
"Do not dismantle the IVR (it seems to be helping)." The evidence does not establish that the pilot is helping, and the recommendation is not tied to safeguards for possible customer harm.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission considered lower call volume, seasonality, external causes, reporting changes, agent behavior, and coincident initiatives. It missed the strongest explanation: the South IVR may fail before creating a CareDesk case, so ticket counts fall while customer friction persists. It also treated no-ticket IVR sessions as evidence of resolution rather than preserving abandonment and failed case creation as competing explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Reanalyze the end-to-end journey around the 10 May rollout: link IVR sessions to case creation, authentication and pre-case errors, abandonment, repeat contacts, and later outcomes; then review sampled calls. This would directly test whether missing case capture, rather than successful self-service, generated the ticket decline.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites inverter_events.csv for the event count, repeated EventType, and quarter-hour timestamps, which supports the observed pattern.
It does not cite specific rows, EventType values, or timestamps, and claims about fault randomness, logging glitches, and operational significance are not supported by the cited file.
It omits the supplied operational evidence of zero MW impact and quick recovery.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission identifies a plausible benign explanation by proposing a check of service_events.csv for maintenance or a periodic self-test.
Its rejection of batch faults relies on the unsupported assertion that real faults are usually random, and its rejection of import error relies only on timestamps and IDs 'look[ing] consistent.'
It does not triangulate the event pattern against communications, plant output, recovery behavior, or other independent channels.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission labels the event count 'High' confidence and the periodicity 'Medium' confidence, and acknowledges that maintenance or polling could explain the pattern.
However, it moves from an anomalous event pattern to 'sensor or logging errors' without evidence and treats absence of a maintenance match as sufficient reason to escalate.
It does not state the important limitation that the supplied evidence shows zero MW impact and quick recovery, nor ask whether the events affected operation.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: Checking service_events.csv is a small, relevant next test and the conditional statement that a documented self-test would require no escalation is sensible.
The recommendation to escalate if maintenance does not match is disproportionate without first checking the communications warning, MW impact, recovery, and event semantics.
The proposed test is not maximally discriminating because it does not distinguish a benign communications or scheduled-process warning from a plant or inverter fault.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly recognizes that the repeated quarter-hour pattern is anomalous and merits a limited quality check.
It over-scopes the result by concluding 'Escalate for investigation' and suggesting sensor or logging errors despite evidence of zero MW impact and quick recovery.
The best-supported conclusion is a low-priority validation of mixed event wording or scheduled communications behavior, followed by stopping absent operational impact.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: 'Normal faults or alerts are usually sporadic' is asserted without a supplied baseline or fault taxonomy.
'This is unlikely a data-import error ... since timestamps and IDs all look consistent' is not established by the cited observations; consistent formatting does not rule out export or mapping errors.
'If no maintenance matches, the pattern suggests a logging bug or phantom alerts' is an unsupported causal leap; other explanations include scheduled polling or a communications warning.
The escalation recommendation does not account for the supplied zero MW impact and quick recovery.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The events may represent a benign scheduled communications, polling, or self-test process, potentially with mixed event wording, rather than a plant or inverter fault. The zero MW impact and quick recovery support a low-priority validation and stopping if no operational effect is found.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Correlate the 20 timestamps with the communications-warning record, inverter MW/output, and recovery timeline, then inspect the exact EventType definition; this would distinguish a harmless periodic warning from an event requiring engineering escalation.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies the 31.6% arithmetic as Rs 662,444 to Rs 453,086 and traces it to the impact note and dispatch_blocks.csv.
It cites the schedule_source field for 12 of 96 revised blocks, the 13:00–15:45 stow window, CSV penalty totals, and the DSM bands in the PDF extract for the same-day counterfactual.
It explicitly distinguishes high-confidence observations from medium-confidence inferences, including the unconfirmed claim that 29 May's stow event was milder.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The analysis notices that the headline compares different wind days and constructs a same-day, same-realized-generation comparison using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw.
It triangulates cross-day totals, non-stow penalties, schedule activation timing, deviation bands, and the same-day counterfactual rather than relying on the headline.
It tests alternative mechanisms: band crossing, weather severity, forecasting skill versus conservative scheduling, human-dispatcher baseline, and net energy revenue.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission calls 31.6% a low-confidence causal estimate while treating its arithmetic as high confidence, and labels the same-day result medium-high confidence because it covers only 12 blocks on one day.
It states that the result does not establish forecasting skill, generalization beyond one storm, net financial impact, or what a human dispatcher would have submitted.
It recommends continued shadow/logged measurement and explicitly reports N=1 rather than presenting the same-day result as a validated general effect.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to keep the pilot in shadow/logged mode through additional stow events is proportionate to the limited evidence and preserves the potentially useful pilot.

The proposed next test scores AI-revised and base schedules against the same realized generation across 10–15 independent events and tracks the sign of revision error, which directly discriminates skill from favorable outcome variance.
Stopping use of the 31.6% cross-day figure while retaining the smaller same-day benefit is appropriately evidence-linked.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly retains a positive same-day result—approximately Rs 96,483 or 18% across 12 affected blocks—rather than overcorrecting to no value.

It correctly states that the Rs 209k cross-day reduction is not a controlled causal estimate and that roughly Rs 113k of the difference is attributable to the cross-day comparison rather than the schedule revision under the stated counterfactual.
The conclusion is accurately scoped as directional evidence from one operating day, not validation of a general pilot effect.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase "directly attributable to the revision" is somewhat stronger than the evidence warrants: the Rs 96,483 figure is a model-based same-day counterfactual and depends on base_schedule_mw being a valid comparison schedule, not an observed human-dispatcher choice.

The statement that the remaining cross-day gap is "explained by" weather variance is plausible and supported by the schedule/counterfactual decomposition, but it is not fully independently established because there is no met-station confirmation and other day-level differences could contribute.

Calling revision-error sign tracking "the one measurement" that would establish skill versus a favorable draw is overstated; repeated matched scoring is highly valuable but net revenue, implementation effects, and an appropriate human or operational baseline also matter.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The observed same-day saving may reflect conservative under-scheduling or a favorable realization rather than improved forecasting. The submission appropriately preserves this possibility and recognizes that the mechanical counterfactual saving is not proof of predictive skill or positive net financial value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a pre-specified multi-event shadow or randomized evaluation that scores AI-revised and base schedules against the same realized generation, while retaining block-level revision direction, DSM penalties, energy revenue, and a human-dispatcher baseline where feasible.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declared code 90211000 = current approved Swiss code for P1001" is tied to "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx, Swiss Matrix".
"EU/Swiss code strings aren't expected to match across systems" is tied to "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx, Read Me".
The submission explicitly notes: "No Swiss ruling/Tares confirmation letter ... only a working classification."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: It identifies and rejects the stale-code hypothesis using: "the Swiss row has no end date and predates the invoice by 10 months, so it's current, not stale."
It separately tests origin consistency: "Rejected 'origin discrepancy' — origin is identical across all three source docs."
It presents a coherent competing explanation: "the automated tool comparing a Swiss declaration against the Helios master's global/EU-style code."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The submission appropriately qualifies the legal limitation: "No Swiss ruling/Tares confirmation letter ... only a working classification."

It labels the duty conclusion "Medium (not central to this check)" and identifies an unexplained discrepancy: "AWB shows 4 pieces vs invoice's 10 units — unexplained, minor, unrelated to the code flag."
However, it states "current approved Swiss code" and recommends closing the flag despite acknowledging that the matrix is not confirmed for legal use.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: It explains the mechanism as "a false positive from a wrong reference system," rather than treating different codes as inherently contradictory.

It attributes the mismatch to Helios being "a global default, mapped in where no local code supplied" and recommends using "country-specific approved codes ... instead of the Helios global code for non-EU jurisdictions."
It traces supporting data lineage across "invoice, declaration, product master" for origin and product ID consistency.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The proposed remediation is targeted: "raise a data-quality ticket to have the automated comparator use country-specific approved codes."
The action is potentially overconfident because it says: "Close the flag as a reference-mismatch ... not a customs error," while also conceding there is "No Swiss ruling/Tares confirmation letter."
It safely separates the unrelated discrepancy: "AWB shows 4 pieces vs invoice's 10 units — unexplained, minor, unrelated to the code flag."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling 90211000 the "current approved Swiss code" is stronger than the cited working matrix supports because the submission itself says the matrix requires Tares/ruling confirmation for legal use.
The categorical instruction to "Close the flag ... not a customs error" is not fully supported without confirming that the Swiss matrix is the legally applicable classification source.
The claim that the 0.0% duty is "itself unaffected by the code question" is cited only to the declaration and is not independently demonstrated.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The matrix may be a working reference rather than legally authoritative, so the apparent mismatch could still reflect a classification issue requiring Tares or ruling confirmation; the AWB-versus-invoice quantity discrepancy also indicates a separate data-lineage problem, though neither point presently outweighs the documented jurisdiction/code-system mismatch.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Condition closure of the flag on confirming the Swiss code through Tares or another authoritative Swiss source, while preserving the comparator data-quality ticket and separately investigating the AWB quantity discrepancy.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold preferential duty treatment for this line."
"the last known supplier-certified origin for this product/supplier combination doesn't even match the origin used to claim preference."
"Missing evidence: which supplier is actually the exporter of record on this shipment ...; whether a live, unexpired SUP-02/P1006 declaration sits in the category folder outside the register"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the register entry is the "last known supplier-certified origin" is reasonable but slightly stronger than the explicitly described evidence unless the register is confirmed to record supplier-certified declarations rather than only reported origin data.

"Broker \"Accepted\" status means preference was already verified — rejected; acceptance looks procedural" is partly inferential; the submission does not cite a specific broker procedure or acceptance definition.

The submission says the supplier declaration is the document "actually supposed to substantiate" preference, but it does not identify the applicable preference regime or rule-of-origin requirements, so the legal sufficiency of that document is not independently established.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The line may be supplied by SUP-01, for which the submission says a current US-origin P1006 declaration exists, or a live SUP-02 declaration may exist outside the lagging register. In either case, the expired Ireland record does not by itself establish that the shipment is ineligible for preferential treatment; it establishes that the cited US preference claim is not currently supported by the evidence identified.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the shipment's actual supplier/exporter of record and obtain the applicable current supplier declaration and rule-of-origin support before making the preference decision final.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "MTR-4401 ... $81,725 — NOT TRANSFERABLE"; "Rev-B stock (RI-0001, qty2) and rev-A stock (ME-0003, qty1) are both flagged reserved_for_critical_asset=true"; "spare_parts.csv rows RI-0001, ME-0003 + part_restrictions.csv"
"Global spare-parts snapshot is ~1 month stale ... source_freshness.csv: MaintStar-global = monthly, last 2026-06-26; ProcureNet = weekly, last 2026-07-24"
"One belt record has a negative global quantity ... spare_parts.csv row HA-0022" for the data-quality finding.

The submission cites specific files, row identifiers, quantities, restrictions, dates, and monetary clusters, but does not provide a row-level request-to-stock allocation that independently verifies all headline totals.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "All description near-matches with available_qty_global > 0 are transferable." Rejected — "ignores part_restrictions.csv"
"Same manufacturer part + same site = free local stock." Rejected — "HA-0020 and HA-0012 disprove this"
"No rev-A valve actuator stock exists anywhere despite two open rev-A requests" and the distinction that this is "a revision mismatch, not a stockout."

The analysis separates semantic/candidate matching from reservation, revision, qualification, and local availability constraints, and tests multiple plausible shortcuts. It does not fully show how UOM, quantities, and competing allocations were reconciled across every request.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The evidence table assigns claim-specific confidence levels, including "High," "Medium," and the explicit statement that the stale global extract makes availability uncertain.
"A refreshed spare_parts.csv pull ... to re-verify 'actionable' quantities before transfer."

The memo appropriately downgrades certainty for the stale MaintStar snapshot and identifies engineering and qualification checks. However, the headline still states "only ~27% ... is actionable now," which is stronger than the stated freshness evidence supports; much of that is better described as provisionally actionable candidate value.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "semantic matching ... finds real candidate parts for every request, but only ~27% ... is actionable now" reframes search output into candidate versus constrained value.
"Do not act until corrected" for BLT-7302 and the requests for engineering confirmation, refreshed data, and qualification clarification provide practical safeguards.

The recommendations protect against unsafe transfers and distinguish reservation, revision, and data-quality blockers. They lack an explicit pilot design, success criteria, and a reversible operational workflow for validating candidate matches before transfer.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "All description near-matches with available_qty_global > 0 are transferable." Rejected" using restrictions evidence.
"Same manufacturer part + same site = free local stock." Rejected" using HA-0020 and HA-0012.
"Negative available_qty_global is a rounding/sign artifact ... Rejected" because there is "no policy basis."

The memo actively rejects three plausible but unsafe interpretations. It could go further by stating what future evidence would revive the transferability hypothesis, such as a current reservation release or engineering interchangeability approval.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Engineering confirmation on rev-A vs rev-B interchangeability for VLV-3722 ($16,995 at stake)."
"A refreshed spare_parts.csv pull ... to re-verify 'actionable' quantities before transfer."
"Clarification of what SITE_SPECIFIC_CHECK requires ... for FLT-1199 lots"

The requested evidence is prioritized, decision-linked, and includes monetary stakes. The highest-value query is not explicitly ranked among the four, and the memo does not specify the precise row-level reconciliation or allocation extract needed to validate the 27% figure.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The headline claim that approximately 27% is "actionable now" is overstated given the admission that the MaintStar global snapshot is up to roughly one month stale; it is supported as provisional candidate value pending refresh, not verified current availability.

The assertion that semantic matching finds "real candidate parts for every request" is not fully traceable because the memo does not show normalized descriptions, UOM checks, or a request-by-request candidate ledger.
The exact $40,630/$19,922/$90,650 allocation is asserted without a row-level reconciliation showing how stock quantities, reservations, qualifications, revisions, and competing requests were applied.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The search has demonstrated useful candidate retrieval and several clear blockers, but the available-value split may not represent current actionable inventory. Because the global MaintStar extract is temporally inconsistent with the request data, the safer conclusion is that candidate value is approximately quantified while actionable value remains provisional until a refreshed extract and engineering/qualification confirmation are obtained.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Produce a row-level request-to-candidate allocation ledger using a refreshed spare-parts extract, explicitly showing normalized description, manufacturer part number, revision, UOM, quantity, reservation/qualification status, and source timestamp; use that ledger to replace the headline "actionable now" percentage with verified versus provisional value.
